newsitem.title: USA: Oakmark manager eyes stocks not countries-Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Oakmark manager eyes stocks not countries-Barron's.

text.p: International fund manager David Herro, who runs the $1.6 billion Oakmark International Fund and the Oakmark International Small Cap, said his investment team looked for foreign companies rather than markets which would outperform, Barron's said.
But even when using a set of stock selection criteria, certain geographical biases appeared, the investor weekly newspaper said in its May 26 edition.
Herro said he continued to have a light weighting in Japan and did not have a strongly bullish outlook on the market, Barron's reported.
"The point about Japan is that I believe it is out of sync in terms of value to us as owners of business," Herro was quoted as saying.
Herro looked for companies selling at a cheap price relative to cash flow and for management whose aim was to build shareholder value, Barron's said.
Sweden merited a higher weighting, he said.

"In that country, you have a number of high-quality multinational companies that are extremely well-run and, for the most part, run with shareholder interest in mind," he said, pointing to AB Volvo as an example.
Right now, Herro was focused on Great Britain, Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong and Sweden, Barron's said.
Leading his list of favorites is Malaysian cellular phone company Technology Resources Industries Bhd. In Britain, he liked Cordiant plc, Sedwick Group and sugar refiner Tate and Lyle, Barron's said.
His investment team eliminated countries deemed unsafe or which lacked proper investor regulations, like Russia. They avoided direct investment in Chinese companies, Barron's said.
